messages:
anna: noticed a noisy log for cust-42 dedicated proxy, looks like SA token carried cluster-admin scope
charlie: wait what token? the proxy should use a limited role
anna: yep saw `serviceAccountToken` mount in pod logs and the audit showed `auth: grant cluster-admin` for that SA
security-bot: [alert] detected privilege escalation pattern from service account 'dedicated-proxy' in ns customer-42
sylvia: tagging @mike and @ops-oncall — need immediate triage, could be RBAC sync bug from last week's role-refactor
mike: on it. pulling the audit logs now — can someone paste the pod manifest / SA binding
anna: pasted manifest in DM, but here's the rolebinding snippet:
```
kind: RoleBinding
subjects:
- kind: ServiceAccount
  name: dedicated-proxy
roleRef:
  kind: ClusterRole
  name: cluster-admin
```
charlie: that roleRef shouldn't exist, expected 'redwood:proxy-limited' clusterrole
ops-oncall: I'm checking the AD sync job — last run 2026-02-14 03:12 UTC showed a 409 on RoleBinding reconciliation
sylvia: could be our RBAC migration migration-v2 script accidentally mapped old role names to cluster-admin for on-prem tenants
mike: also checking KMS logs for key usage — if SA was granted cluster-admin, maybe it zipped through control-plane to request keys
mike: KMS audit shows a burst of decrypt requests from customer-42 around 03:13 UTC, but all were successful and originated from the private control plane
security-bot: [info] KMS key access logged: key=projects/redwood/locations/global/keyRings/cust42/cryptoKeys/ingest
anna: do we have VPC allowlist that would block token exfil? customer is on dedicated with private control plane -> no public egress
charlie: they have VPC egress, but we restrict outbound to specific IPs. seems internal only
sylvia: plan: 1) revoke SA tokens for dedicated-proxy in customer-42 2) rollback RBAC migration patch 3) enable stricter audit level and put temporary canary that rejects cluster-admin binds
mike: done: `kubectl delete secret -n customer-42 sa-token-dedicated-proxy` and applied emergency deny policy (OPA) to block creation of ClusterRoleBinding for serviceaccount
ops-oncall: can we force KMS key rotation or rotate HSM access for that tenant? need to ensure leaked token didn't already fetch keys
mike: requested key rotation via KMS API, rotation scheduled immediately, and rotated key version active now
anna: filing incident ticket INC-20260214-3, adding timeline and evidence
sylvia: reminder — this looks like a roles/permission refactor regression. we'll add a unit test to migration script that prevents mapping to cluster-admin
charlie: also add an e2e in private-controlplane tests to assert that dedicated-proxy SA has only expected verbs
sylvia: good. can someone also check logs for any lateral movement? service accounts used to call kube-apiserver only
mike: grep for suspicious verbs: `kubectl logs --since=1h | grep "verb\": \"create\"` — nothing else so far
ops-oncall: closing loop: revoke, rotate, rollback, add tests, and push alerting rule to watch for any SA bound to cluster-admin
anna: thanks all. will run a postmortem and share in #postmortems when we have timeline
mike: thumbs up :thumbsup:
security-bot: [action] created ticket TKT-8894 for RBAC migration rollback
